nodes.label: ACID Guarantee Set (G1-G5)
nodes.rationale: G1 atomic, G2 reversible (pre-promote hash), G3 isolated (interference budget + router canary), G4 durable cross-session hash, G5 auditable provenance; a metaphor for the guarantee set, not DB-ACID.

nodes.label: Router-Integrity Invariant (G3)
nodes.rationale: The router is treated as an invariant with a canary set so locality and abstention stay measurable; without it revoke is a router trick (the SEUF/GRIP failure mode).

nodes.label: State-Identity Revocation (G2)
nodes.rationale: revoke(id) restores the pre-promote state hash, bitwise on the arithmetic path; hash identity is bookkeeping, so the load-bearing measurement is behavioural return (canary KL, retain accuracy).

nodes.label: Transaction Ledger
nodes.rationale: Append-only ledger {id, kind, provenance, hash, parent state}; state = H(H0, L) so every write is auditable and any can be revoked back to the pre-promote hash. The system property, not a new block, is the contribution.
